title: Lámina Anatómica
idiom: anatomical plate: specimen, numbered callouts, key, engraved hatching
rule: One fitting-module is drawn forty times on a standing body that is never drawn, and the forty numbers are placed on an Archimedean spiral (r = 262 + 6.0i, theta = 0.62i) so the sequence is a rotation, not a list; fitting 21 is inverted (the break).

readings.far: a technical anatomical plate: a hatched field, a symmetric specimen, a ring of numbered stations, a key at the foot
readings.middle: an exploded heart-pump with filter lungs, a boiler skull, a flanged spine, ribs and a plinth, circled by a spiral of forty numbers
readings.near: seven-segment numerals as drawn paths; forty fittings whose leader terminals trace a standing body; the boiler's twelve rivets; the key's rectangular spiral of forty cells; the shadow cross-hatching

techniques: generative numbering: forty stations on an Archimedean spiral, not a list
callout leaders ending on a hidden standing body (head, arms, trunk, legs)
the parts are an exploded machine-organism: bellows heart, filter lungs, boiler skull, flanged spine
seven-segment numerals drawn as vector paths (no text element)
engraved ground: 150 rule lines, a nervous grid, cross-hatched shadow
the key as a second spiral (rectangular), forty cells
statement: A plate of a body made of its own instruments. Forty fittings are numbered on a widening spiral and sited on a standing frame that is never engraved: the heart is a pump, the lungs are filters, the skull is a boiler, and if you follow the leaders in order the fittings draw the man.
